The audit

{{n_checks_cap}} checks, {{n_datasets}} published benchmarks, and {{n_pass_with_train_word}} that nothing was flagged on.

We pointed the tool at the benchmarks people already train on. {{n_collections_cap}} collections, curated into one format and put through the same {{n_checks_word}} checks — so these are measurements on published data, browsable per dataset, with the report behind every number.

  • {{n_datasets}} Datasets audited, across {{n_collections_word}} collections Curated from {{n_curated}}; {{n_excluded}} could not be put through the same {{n_checks_word}} checks
  • {{n_fail}} Flagged Fail on at least one of the {{n_checks_word}} checks {{n_warning}} rolled up to Warning, {{n_pass}} to Pass
  • {{median_probe_auroc}} Median AUROC recovered by one hand-crafted feature on its own {{n_probe_over_0_7}} of the {{n_probed}} probed datasets reach 0.70 or more from one feature
  • {{n_leakage_over_50}} Datasets where half or more of the held-out split is also in training {{n_with_any_leakage}} of the {{n_leakage_scanned}} scanned have at least one sequence in two splits

{{n_pass_with_train_cap}} of the {{n_with_train}} datasets that define a training split had nothing flagged on any check. That is not a statement about the rest, and a Pass is not a guarantee about a dataset: it establishes that these {{n_checks_word}} checks do not separate the classes, so every number above is a lower bound on what a learned model could recover. A check reports what it measured and not what caused it, and a compositional difference between classes may be genuine biology.

The aggregate is not the useful part. What tells you what to control for is the name of the feature that separated your benchmark and the distribution it was measured on — so the audit is published per dataset, not as a headline. That is what the rest of this page is.

Every dataset, every check

{{n_datasets}} rows by {{n_checks}} columns, grouped by collection and ordered worst-first inside each group. This is the whole audit on one surface, and it is the way into the rest of the site: every mark is a link. Narrow it to a collection, or to the flag a dataset rolled up to, and the rows that are left are the ones worth reading.

{{fig_flag_matrix}}

Each cell is the flag that check returned on that dataset’s reference split — train for all but one of them, never a maximum taken over splits. Why one split is quoted.
